How Skill Loom carries a chain from a project folder to a guarded run

Long image

A

Answer

Skill Loom is a local owner process. The CLI and companion skills ask it to author chains, preflight them, and run one chain at a time under review.

  1. The owner is the only process that writes project state or spawns a harness.
  2. Every mutating start needs a review digest and explicit confirmations; an authored skill is staged and installed only after a separate approval.
  3. One active run per profile; tails are bounded and recovery is explicit.
  4. Harness differences live in adapters, not in routes or runners.

Applies toRepository at 122fdc85managed service, portable path, and per-gap authoring

1

What is the system made of?

The browser only edits chains. Everything else crosses the CLI or a companion skill, and the owner process holds the filesystem and process privileges.

2

What happens from a folder to a finished run?

Each lane is a hand-off, not an automatic continuation. Validity, preflight, and the reviewed digest are separate gates, so a failure returns you to the lane that owns it.

Diagram structure
  • Install and start install
  • Register project project
  • Inspect skill catalog catalog
  • Create or copy chain draft
  • Edit in browser edit
  • Validate chain validate
  • Run preflight preflight
  • Review start digest review
  • Start run start
  • Execute steps execute
  • Run complete done
  • Export or import bundle share
  • catalog → draft · skills fit
  • done → share · bundle
  • draft → edit
  • edit → validate
  • execute → done · last step
  • install → project
  • preflight → review · gates pass
  • project → catalog
  • review → start · digest confirmed
  • start → execute
  • validate → preflight · valid
3

How does a missing skill become part of the chain?

An optional branch closes one gap at a time. Existing steps stay valid, and an instruction-only step remains the fallback. The audit is advisory, not a safety gate; ADR-00291 records the policy.

  1. Record the gap

    Name the step role, the sources searched, and why an instruction is not enough.

  2. Stage with skill-creator

    Scaffold at <project>/.skill-loom-authored/<name>/; at most three per chain.

  3. Audit with skill-review

    Scope the audit to the staged package; the score is advisory.

  4. Install after approval

    Validate, fingerprint, and install without overwrite.

  5. Re-resolve the chain

    Refresh the catalog and re-check every step name before packaging.

4

Where is each guard enforced when a run starts?

The control server checks the token and request shape. The orchestrator then re-runs preflight and compares the reviewed digest before it claims the single slot. The owner writes the frozen snapshot before the first process starts.

Diagram structure
  • CLI cli
  • Control server control
  • Orchestrator orch
  • Preflight engine pre
  • Run owner owner
  • Run store store
  • PTY and harness pty
  • cli → control · JSON line and bearer token
  • control → orch · run.start
  • orch → pre · re-run preflight
  • pre → orch · report and acknowledgements
  • orch → owner · digest ok, claim slot
  • owner → store · frozen snapshot and pointer
  • owner → pty · spawn shell-free
  • pty → owner · output and exit or OSC 7501
  • owner → store · step state and bounded tail
  • orch → control · RunView and events
  • control → cli · JSON response or events
5

What can a run be, and how does it move?

starting covers snapshot and claim. awaiting-user is the supervised hand-off after a step ends; automatic runs skip it. Recovery from interrupted writes a new starting state and never replays a completed step.

Diagram structure
  • Starting starting
  • Running running
  • Awaiting user awaiting-user
  • Paused paused
  • Interrupted interrupted
  • Completed completed
  • Failed failed
  • Aborted aborted
  • starting → running · runner starts
  • running → completed · last step done
  • running → awaiting-user · step ends
  • awaiting-user → running · done or next
  • running → paused · pause or timeout
  • paused → running · resume
  • running → failed · explicit failure
  • running → aborted · abort
  • awaiting-user → aborted · abort
  • paused → aborted · abort
  • starting → interrupted · restart
  • running → interrupted · restart
  • awaiting-user → interrupted · restart
  • paused → interrupted · restart
  • interrupted → starting · retry, continue, or restart

What is still blocked or unverified?

Do not read these as working paths

Protected managed skill execution is blocked until a verified content view exists. Descendant containment is unverified on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Automatic OpenCode CLI starts remain blocked; one single-step probe passed on 2.2.6. Windows PowerShell 7 behavior is implemented but not verified. A portable run cannot prepare a bundle that selects a native agent. Managed discovery workspaces cannot carry locally authored skills.

12

What changed since the November 6 page?

That page predates the CLI and skill pivot in cfbf981. Its service-first framing still centers the server and editor. The current web surface is the chain editor only; projects, catalogs, discovery, workspaces, and runs are CLI- or skill-driven. Since 343fda3, ADR-0029 adds the explicit per-gap authoring branch: scenario-discovery can hand one gap to skill-creator, scope skill-review to the staged package, and install only after approval.

13

Where are the deeper views?

The companion pages open beside this one. chain-save-sequence.html follows the editor save from PUT to atomic rename. portable-handoff-workflow.html follows a bundle that runs without the service, including bundles that mix pinned candidates and reviewed local skills. Both pages come from the same repository revision.
